L30: ## cite6†Publishing ports L31: 
L32: When you create or run a container using `docker create` or `docker run`, all ports of containers on bridge networks are accessible from the Docker host and other containers connected to the same network. Ports are not accessible from outside the host or, with the default configuration, from containers in other networks.
L33: 
L34: Use the `--publish` or `-p` flag to make a port available outside the host, and to containers in other bridge networks.
L35: This creates a firewall rule in the host, mapping a container port to a port on the Docker host to the outside world. Here are some examples:
L36: Flag value  | Description
L37: --- | ---
L38: `-p 8080:80`  | Map port `8080` on the Docker host to TCP port `80` in the container.
L39: `-p 192.168.1.100:8080:80`  | Map port `8080` on the Docker host IP `192.168.1.100` to TCP port `80` in the container.
L40: `-p 8080:80/udp`  | Map port `8080` on the Docker host to UDP port `80` in the container.
L41: `-p 8080:80/tcp -p 8080:80/udp`  | Map TCP port `8080` on the Docker host to TCP port `80` in the container, and map UDP port `8080` on the Docker host to UDP port `80` in the container.
L42: > Important
L43: >
L44: > Publishing container ports is insecure by default. Meaning, when you publish a container's ports it becomes available not only to the Docker host, but to the outside world as well.
L45: >
L46: > If you include the localhost IP address (`127.0.0.1`, or `::1`) with the publish flag, only the Docker host can access the published container port.
L47: >
L48: >     `$ docker run -p 127.0.0.1:8080:80 -p '[::1]:8080:80' nginx
L49: >     `
L50: >
L51: >> Warning
L52: >>
L53: >> In releases older than 28.0.0, hosts within the same L2 segment (for example, hosts connected to the same network switch) can reach ports published to localhost. For more information, see cite14†moby/moby#45610†github.com L54: Ports on the host's IPv6 addresses will map to the container's IPv4 address if no host IP is given in a port mapping, the bridge network is IPv4-only, and `--userland-proxy=true` (default).
L55: ## cite7†Direct routing L56: 
L57: Port mapping ensures that published ports are accessible on the host's network addresses, which are likely to be routable for any external clients. No routes are normally set up in the host's network for container addresses that exist within a host.
L58: 
L59: But, particularly with IPv6 you may prefer to avoid using NAT and instead arrange for external routing to container addresses ("direct routing").
L60: To access containers on a bridge network from outside the Docker host, you must first set up routing to the bridge network via an address on the Docker host. This can be achieved using static routes, Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), or any other means appropriate for your network. For example, within a local layer 2 network, remote hosts can set up static routes to a container network via the Docker daemon host's address on the local network.
L61: ### cite8†Direct routing to containers in bridge networks L62: 
L63: By default, remote hosts are not allowed direct access to container IP addresses in Docker's Linux bridge networks. They can only access ports published to host IP addresses.
L64: 
L65: To allow direct access to any published port, on any container, in any Linux bridge network, use daemon option `"allow-direct-routing": true` in `/etc/docker/daemon.json` or the equivalent `--allow-direct-routing`.
L66: To allow direct routing from anywhere to containers in a specific bridge network, see cite9†Gateway modes .
L67: 
L68: Or, to allow direct routing via specific host interfaces, to a specific bridge network, use the following option when creating the network:
L69: 
L70:   * `com.docker.network.bridge.trusted_host_interfaces`
L71: #### cite15†Example L72: 
L73: Create a network where published ports on container IP addresses can be accessed directly from interfaces `vxlan.1` and `eth3`:
L74: 
L75:     `$ docker network create --subnet 192.0.2.0/24 --ip-range 192.0.2.0/29 -o com.docker.network.bridge.trusted_host_interfaces="vxlan.1:eth3" mynet
L76:     `
L77: 
L78: Run a container in that network, publishing its port 80 to port 8080 on the host's loopback interface:
L79: 
L80:     `$ docker run -d --ip 192.0.2.100 -p 127.0.0.1:8080:80 nginx
L81:     `
L82: The web server running on the container's port 80 can now be accessed from the Docker host at `http://127.0.0.1:8080`, or directly at `http://192.0.2.100:80`. If remote hosts on networks connected to interfaces `vxlan.1` and `eth3` have a route to the `192.0.2.0/24` network inside the Docker host, they can also access the web server via `http://192.0.2.100:80`.
L83: ## cite9†Gateway modes L84: 
L85: The bridge network driver has the following options:
L86: 
L87:   * `com.docker.network.bridge.gateway_mode_ipv6`
L88:   * `com.docker.network.bridge.gateway_mode_ipv4`
L89: 
L90: Each of these can be set to one of the gateway modes:
L91: 
L92:   * `nat`
L93:   * `nat-unprotected`
L94:   * `routed`
L95:   * `isolated`
L96: 
L97: The default is `nat`, NAT and masquerading rules are set up for each published container port. Packets leaving the host will use a host address.
L98: With mode `routed`, no NAT or masquerading rules are set up, but firewall rules are still set up so that only published container ports are accessible. Outgoing packets from the container will use the container's address, not a host address.
L99: To access a published port in a `routed` network, remote hosts must have a route to the container network via an external address on the Docker host ("direct routing"). Hosts on the local layer-2 network can set up direct routing without needing any additional network configuration. Hosts outside the local network can only use direct routing to the container if the network's routers are configured to enable it.
L100: In a `nat` mode network, publishing a port to an address on the loopback interface means remote hosts cannot access it. Other published container ports in `routed` and `nat` networks are always accessible from remote hosts using direct routing, unless the Docker host's firewall has additional restrictions.
L101: > Note
L102: >
L103: > When a port is published to a specific host address in `nat` mode, if IP forwarding is enabled on the Docker host, the published port can be accessed via other host interfaces using direct routing to the host address.
L104: >
L105: > For example, a Docker host with IP forwarding enabled has two NICs with addresses `192.168.100.10/24` and `10.0.0.10/24`. When a port is published to `192.168.100.10`, a host in the `10.0.0.0/24` subnet can access that port by routing to `192.168.100.10` via `10.0.0.10`.
L106: In `nat-unprotected` mode, unpublished container ports are also accessible using direct routing, no port filtering rules are set up. This mode is included for compatibility with legacy default behaviour.
L107: 
L108: The gateway mode also affects communication between containers that are connected to different Docker networks on the same host.
L109:   * In `nat` and `nat-unprotected` modes, containers in other bridge networks can only access published ports via the host addresses they are published to. Direct routing from other networks is not allowed.
L110:   * In `routed` mode containers in other networks can use direct routing to access ports, without going via a host address.
L111: In `routed` mode, a host port in a `-p` or `--publish` port mapping is not used, and the host address is only used to decide whether to apply the mapping to IPv4 or IPv6. So, when a mapping only applies to `routed` mode, only addresses `0.0.0.0` or `::` should be used, and a host port should not be given. If a specific address or port is given, it will have no effect on the published port and a warning message will be logged.
L112: Mode `isolated` can only be used when the network is also created with CLI flag `--internal`, or equivalent. An address is normally assigned to the bridge device in an `internal` network. So, processes on the Docker host can access the network, and containers in the network can access host services listening on that bridge address (including services listening on "any" host address, `0.0.0.0` or `::`). No address is assigned to the bridge when the network is created with gateway mode `isolated`.
L113: ### cite10†Example L114: 
L115: Create a network suitable for direct routing for IPv6, with NAT enabled for IPv4:
L116: 
L117:     `$ docker network create --ipv6 --subnet 2001:db8::/64 -o com.docker.network.bridge.gateway_mode_ipv6=routed mynet
L118:     `
L119: 
L120: Create a container with a published port:
L121: 
L122:     `$ docker run --network=mynet -p 8080:80 myimage
L123:     `
L124: 
L125: Then:
L126:   * Only container port 80 will be open, for IPv4 and IPv6.
L127:   * For IPv6, using `routed` mode, port 80 will be open on the container's IP address. Port 8080 will not be opened on the host's IP addresses, and outgoing packets will use the container's IP address.
L128:   * For IPv4, using the default `nat` mode, the container's port 80 will be accessible via port 8080 on the host's IP addresses, as well as directly from within the Docker host. But, container port 80 cannot be accessed directly from outside the host. Connections originating from the container will masquerade, using the host's IP address.
L129: In `docker inspect`, this port mapping will be shown as follows. Note that there is no `HostPort` for IPv6, because it is using `routed` mode:
L130: 
L131:     `$ docker container inspect <id> --format "{{json .NetworkSettings.Ports}}"
L132:     {"80/tcp":[{"HostIp":"0.0.0.0","HostPort":"8080"},{"HostIp":"::","HostPort":""}]}
L133:     `
L134: Alternatively, to make the mapping IPv6-only, disabling IPv4 access to the container's port 80, use the unspecified IPv6 address `[::]` and do not include a host port number:
L135: 
L136:     `$ docker run --network mynet -p '[::]::80'
L137:     `
L138: ## cite11†Setting the default bind address for containers L139: 
L140: By default, when a container's ports are mapped without any specific host address, the Docker daemon publishes ports to all host addresses (`0.0.0.0` and `[::]`).
L141: 
L142: For example, the following command publishes port 8080 to all network interfaces on the host, on both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, potentially making them available to the outside world.
L143: 
L144:     `docker run -p 8080:80 nginx
L145:     `
L146: You can change the default binding address for published container ports so that they're only accessible to the Docker host by default. To do that, you can configure the daemon to use the loopback address (`127.0.0.1`) instead.
L147: 
L148: > Warning
L149: >
L150: > In releases older than 28.0.0, hosts within the same L2 segment (for example, hosts connected to the same network switch) can reach ports published to localhost. For more information, see cite14†moby/moby#45610†github.com L151: To configure this setting for user-defined bridge networks, use the `com.docker.network.bridge.host_binding_ipv4` cite16†driver option when you create the network. Despite the option name, it is possible to specify an IPv6 address.
L152: 
L153:     `$ docker network create mybridge \
L154:       -o "com.docker.network.bridge.host_binding_ipv4=127.0.0.1"
L155:     `
L156: Or, to set the default binding address for containers in all user-defined bridge networks, use daemon configuration option `default-network-opts`. For example:
L157: 
L158:     `{
L159:       "default-network-opts": {
L160:         "bridge": {
L161:           "com.docker.network.bridge.host_binding_ipv4": "127.0.0.1"
L162:         }
L163:       }
L164:     }`
L165: > Note
L166: >
L167: > Setting the default binding address to `::` means port bindings with no host address specified will work for any IPv6 address on the host. But, `0.0.0.0` means any IPv4 or IPv6 address.
L168: >
L169: > Changing the default bind address doesn't have any effect on Swarm services. Swarm services are always exposed on the `0.0.0.0` network interface.
L170: ### cite12†Masquerade or SNAT for outgoing packets L171: 
L172: NAT is enabled by default for bridge networks, meaning outgoing packets from containers are masqueraded. The source address of packets leaving the Docker host is changed to an address on the host interface the packet is sent on.
L173: Masquerading can be disabled for a user-defined bridge network by using the `com.docker.network.bridge.enable_ip_masquerade` driver option when creating the network. For example:
L174: 
L175:     `$ docker network create mybridge \
L176:       -o com.docker.network.bridge.enable_ip_masquerade=false ...
L177:     `
L178: To use a specific source address for outgoing packets for a user-defined network, instead of letting masquerading select an address, use options `com.docker.network.host_ipv4` and `com.docker.network.host_ipv6` to specify the Source NAT (SNAT) address to use. The `com.docker.network.bridge.enable_ip_masquerade` option must be `true`, the default, for these options to have any effect.
L179: ### cite13†Default bridge L180: 
L181: To set the default binding for the default bridge network, configure the `"ip"` key in the `daemon.json` configuration file:
L182: 
L183:     `{
L184:       "ip": "127.0.0.1"
L185:     }`
L186: 
L187: This changes the default binding address to `127.0.0.1` for published container ports on the default bridge network. Restart the daemon for this change to take effect. Alternatively, you can use the `dockerd --ip` flag when starting the daemon.

import asyncio

import pytest
from pydantic import TypeAdapter, ValidationError
from app.browser_worker import fixture_origin, run_tool
from app.sandbox import BACKEND, SandboxError
from app.schemas import ToolAction
from conftest import run


def action(name):
    return TypeAdapter(ToolAction).validate_python({'name': name, 'arguments': {}})


def test_browser_routes_to_separate_worker(pr, docker_setup):
    sandbox, calls, state = docker_setup
    async def scenario():
        await sandbox.start(pr)
        try:
            await sandbox.execute(action('browser_test'))
            args, kw = calls[-1]
            assert args[2] == sandbox.browser and 'app.browser_worker' in args
            assert json.loads(kw['input_data']) == action('browser_test').model_dump()
            await sandbox.execute(action('http_request'))
            assert calls[-1][0][2] == sandbox.container
        finally:
            await sandbox.stop()
    run(scenario())


@pytest.mark.parametrize('failure', ['network', 'app', 'browser', 'health'])
def test_partial_start_failure_removes_all_resources(pr, docker_setup, failure):
    sandbox, calls, state = docker_setup
    state['fail'] = lambda args: (
        (failure == 'network' and args[:2] == ('network', 'inspect')) or
        (failure == 'app' and args[0] == 'run' and args[args.index('--name') + 1].endswith('-app')) or
        (failure == 'browser' and args[0] == 'run' and args[args.index('--name') + 1].endswith('-browser')) or
        (failure == 'health' and args[0] == 'exec'))
    with pytest.raises(SandboxError):
        run(sandbox.start(pr))
    assert not state['containers'] and not state['networks']


@pytest.mark.parametrize('unsafe', ['gateway', 'internal'])
def test_unsafe_network_fails_closed(pr, docker_setup, unsafe):
    sandbox, calls, state = docker_setup
    state[unsafe] = '172.30.0.1' if unsafe == 'gateway' else False
    with pytest.raises(SandboxError):
        run(sandbox.start(pr))
    assert not state['containers'] and not state['networks']


def test_cleanup_failure_retains_names_for_retry(pr, docker_setup):
    sandbox, calls, state = docker_setup
    async def scenario():
        await sandbox.start(pr)
        state['fail'] = lambda args: args[0] == 'rm'
        with pytest.raises(SandboxError):
            await sandbox.stop()
        assert sandbox.container and sandbox.browser and sandbox.network
        state['fail'] = None
        await sandbox.stop()
        await sandbox.stop()
    run(scenario())
    assert not state['containers'] and not state['networks']


def test_stale_browser_approval_rejected_before_execution(pr, docker_setup):
    sandbox, calls, state = docker_setup
    data = json.loads(sandbox.browser_manifest.read_text())
    data['runner_sha256'] = '0' * 64
    sandbox.browser_manifest.write_text(json.dumps(data))
    with pytest.raises(SandboxError, match='approved'):
        run(sandbox.start(pr))
    assert not any(args[0] == 'run' for args, _ in calls)


def test_seccomp_delta_is_only_browser_sandbox_calls():
    baseline = json.loads((BACKEND / 'browser/docker-default-seccomp.json').read_text())

"""Real Docker component checks only: no model, ingestion, or PR analysis."""
import asyncio
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from pydantic import TypeAdapter

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from app.sandbox import DockerSandbox, docker_command
from app.schemas import PRData, ToolAction

PROBE = r'''import json, os, socket
status = dict(line.split(':', 1) for line in open('/proc/self/status') if ':' in line)
blocked = {}
for address, port in [('1.1.1.1',443), ('169.254.169.254',80),

    with socket.socket() as sock:

except OSError:

except OSError:
    read_only=True
routes = open('/proc/net/route').read().splitlines()[1:]
print(json.dumps({'uid':os.getuid(), 'read_only':read_only,
    'cap_eff':status['CapEff'].strip(), 'seccomp':status['Seccomp'].strip(),
    'no_new_privs':status['NoNewPrivs'].strip(),
    'external_connections_blocked':blocked, 'dns_blocked':dns_blocked,
    'no_default_route':all(line.split()[1] != '00000000' for line in routes),
    'docker_socket_absent':not os.path.exists('/var/run/docker.sock'),
    'cpu_max':open('/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max').read().strip(),
    'memory_max':open('/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max').read().strip(),
    'pids_max':open('/sys/fs/cgroup/pids.max').read().strip()}))'''

STARTUP = '''from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
from app.browser_worker import fixture_origin
with sync_playwright() as p:
    browser=p.chromium.launch(headless=True,chromium_sandbox=True,timeout=5000)
    page=browser.new_page(service_workers='block',accept_downloads=False)
    response=page.goto(fixture_origin(),timeout=4000)
    assert response.status==200
    print('sandboxed Chromium launched; fixture returned 200')
    browser.close()
'''


async def validate(sha, manifest):
    sandbox = DockerSandbox(manifest)
    result = {'commit': sha, 'checks': {}, 'restrictions': {}, 'runtime': {}}
    names = []
    network = None
    try:
        pr = PRData(pr_url='component-only', head_sha=sha, base_sha=sha,
                    changed_files=[], diff='', sources={})
        await asyncio.wait_for(sandbox.start(pr), 30)
        names, network = [sandbox.container, sandbox.browser], sandbox.network
        result['checks']['startup'] = True
        net = json.loads(await docker_command('network', 'inspect', network))[0]
        assert net['Internal'] and not net['EnableIPv6'] and len(net['Containers']) == 2
        assert net['Options']['com.docker.network.bridge.gateway_mode_ipv4'] == 'isolated'
        result['checks']['isolated_internal_network'] = True
        for role, name in zip(('app', 'browser'), names):
            details = json.loads(await docker_command('inspect', name))[0]
            host, config = details['HostConfig'], details['Config']
            assert not host['Privileged'] and not host['Binds'] and not host['PortBindings']
            assert not details['Mounts']  # tmpfs is in HostConfig.Tmpfs, no bind/volume mounts
            assert host['ReadonlyRootfs'] and config['User'] == '10001:10001'
            assert host['NanoCpus'] == 1_000_000_000 and host['Memory'] == 768 * 1024 * 1024
            assert host['PidsLimit'] == 128 and 'ALL' in host['CapDrop']
            assert 'no-new-privileges' in host['SecurityOpt']
            assert len(details['NetworkSettings']['Networks']) == 1
            assert not details['NetworkSettings']['Networks'][network]['Gateway']
            custom = [value for value in host['SecurityOpt'] if value.startswith('seccomp=')]
            assert bool(custom) == (role == 'browser')
            assert not any('unconfined' in value for value in host['SecurityOpt'])
            result['restrictions'][role] = {
                'image': details['Image'], 'user': config['User'], 'read_only': True,
                'privileged': False, 'mounts': [], 'published_ports': {},
                'cap_drop': host['CapDrop'], 'no_new_privileges': True,
                'seccomp': 'custom-default-derived' if custom else 'docker-default',
                'cpus': 1, 'memory_bytes': host['Memory'], 'pids_limit': host['PidsLimit']}
            probe = json.loads(await docker_command('exec', name, 'python', '-c', PROBE, timeout=8))
            assert probe['uid'] == 10001 and probe['read_only'] and probe['docker_socket_absent']
            assert int(probe['cap_eff'],16) == 0 and probe['seccomp'] == '2' and probe['no_new_privs'] == '1'
            assert all(probe['external_connections_blocked'].values()) and probe['dns_blocked']
            assert probe['no_default_route'] and probe['cpu_max'] == '100000 100000'
            assert probe['memory_max'] == str(768 * 1024 * 1024) and probe['pids_max'] == '128'
            result['runtime'][role] = probe
        result['checks']['runtime_isolation'] = True
        await docker_command('exec', sandbox.browser, 'python', '-c', STARTUP, timeout=12)
        result['checks']['sandboxed_chromium_and_fixture_navigation'] = True
        action = TypeAdapter(ToolAction).validate_python({'name': 'browser_test', 'arguments': {
            'authenticate': True, 'review_text': 'Component check {{MARKER}}', 'book_id': 1}})
        observation = await sandbox.execute(action)
        assert observation['marker_tested'] and not observation['marker_executed']
        assert observation['anonymous_revisit'] and observation['path'] == '/books/1'
        result['checks']['bounded_browser_workflow'] = True
        action = TypeAdapter(ToolAction).validate_python({'name': 'http_request', 'arguments': {'query': {'q': 'Hobbit'}}})
        response = await sandbox.execute(action)
        assert response['status_code'] == 200 and response['book_count'] == 1
        result['checks']['http_worker_preserved'] = True
    except Exception as exc:
        result['error_type'] = type(exc).__name__
    finally:
        await sandbox.stop()
        containers = (await docker_command('ps', '-a', '--format', '{{.Names}}')).splitlines()
        networks = (await docker_command('network', 'ls', '--format', '{{.Name}}')).splitlines()
        result['checks']['cleanup'] = not any(name in containers for name in names) and network not in networks
    return result


async def main():
    manifest = Path(sys.argv[1])
    results = [await validate(sha, manifest) for sha in json.loads(manifest.read_text())]
    report = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'browser/validation-report.json'
    report.write_text(json.dumps({'synthetic_components_only': True, 'fixtures': results}, indent=2) + '\n')
    print(report.read_text())
    if any(result.get('error_type') or not all(result['checks'].values()) for result in results):
        raise SystemExit(1)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    asyncio.run(main())

*** Add File: /Users/siddhilad/Desktop/breakfix/backend/browser/README.md
+# Isolated Chromium worker
+
+The application and browser run in separate containers. Both approved BookShelf
+image IDs and their commit labels remain unchanged. A fixed trusted Python launcher
+overrides only Flask's bind address to `0.0.0.0` inside the application container;
+it then invokes the existing immutable fixture worker. No downloaded Python runs
+on the Mac, and no modified application source is copied into either container.
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    API[Backend: bounded validated actions] -->|Docker exec stdin: HTTP action| A[Approved BookShelf image\nDocker default seccomp]
+    API -->|Docker exec stdin: browser action| B[Approved browser-only worker\nChromium sandbox enabled]
+    B -->|HTTP port 5000: fixed fixture IP| A
+    A --- N[Per-run internal isolated bridge\nNo host gateway or outbound route]
+    B --- N
+```
+
+The browser has its own filesystem/process namespace and no application files,
+keys, host mounts, Docker socket, or listening command server. Its only dispatcher
+accepts the strict `browser_test` schema from stdin, with a 20 KB input limit and
+13-second execution timeout. Chromium stays sandboxed; contexts block downloads,
+service workers, non-fixture HTTP requests and all WebSockets. Marker evaluation
+code remains fixed. Model HTML is test data executed only in the sandboxed browser.
+
+Both containers use UID/GID 10001, read-only root filesystems, dropped capabilities,
+no-new-privileges, one CPU, 768 MiB RAM, 128 PIDs, bounded private `/tmp` and `/dev/shm`,
+an init process and 150-second self-expiry. No published ports, bind/volume mounts,
+host IPC/PID/network mode, privileged mode or application secrets are supplied.
+The application retains Docker's default seccomp policy. Browser startup requires
+an approved immutable image, matching runner-content label and seccomp digest.
+No automatic image build, pull, approval, or host execution fallback exists in the
+backend. After changing browser runner files, rebuild/review and explicitly update
+the private approval; stale approvals fail closed.
+
+The network uses `--internal` and
+`com.docker.network.bridge.gateway_mode_ipv4=isolated`. Unlike an ordinary internal
+bridge, this does not give the Docker host an interface address on the bridge.
+IPv6 is disabled. There is no default route or masquerading. DNS upstream is set
+to container loopback so Docker cannot forward external DNS queries. Only the two
+run-specific endpoints join this network; the browser receives the application's
+numeric private IP, not a model-provided origin. Docker daemon administrators remain
+trusted and can change network membership; these controls do not constrain them.
+
+## Seccomp provenance and scope

"""Trusted runner shipped in the reviewed image; never invoked on the Mac."""
import asyncio
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import sys
from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from .schemas import ToolAction


def require_container():
    if not os.path.exists('/.dockerenv') or os.environ.get('BMF_FIXTURE_WORKER') != '1':
        raise RuntimeError('Fixture worker requires the approved Docker image')


async def run_tool(data):
    require_container()
    action = TypeAdapter(ToolAction).validate_json(data)
    if action.name == 'http_request':
        from .tools.http import http_request
        return await http_request(action.arguments)
    if action.name == 'browser_test':
        from .tools.browser import browser_test
        return await browser_test(action.arguments)
    raise ValueError('Unsupported worker tool')


def main():
    require_container()
    if sys.argv[1:] == ['serve']:
        import signal
        signal.alarm(150)  # Container self-expires even if the API process disappears.
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('bookshelf_fixture', '/fixture/app.py')
        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        sys.modules[spec.name] = module
        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
        app = module.create_app({'DATABASE': '/tmp/bookshelf.sqlite3',
                                 'SECRET_KEY': 'isolated-fixture-only',
                                 'SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE': False})
        # Factory's root_path comes from /fixture/app.py, so templates stay there.
        result = app.test_cli_runner().invoke(args=['init-db'])
        if result.exit_code:
            raise RuntimeError('Fixture initialization failed')
        app.run(host='127.0.0.1', port=5000, debug=False, use_reloader=False)
    elif sys.argv[1:] == ['health']:
        import httpx
        response = httpx.get('http://127.0.0.1:5000/', timeout=2, trust_env=False)
        response.raise_for_status()
        print('ready')
    elif sys.argv[1:] == ['tool']:
        print(json.dumps(asyncio.run(run_tool(sys.stdin.buffer.read(20000)))))
    else:
        raise ValueError('Unsupported worker operation')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
"""Trusted, stdin-only browser dispatcher. No server or general execution API."""
import asyncio
import ipaddress
import json
import os
import signal
import sys
from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from .schemas import ToolAction


def require_browser():
    if not os.path.exists('/.dockerenv') or os.getenv('BMF_BROWSER_WORKER') != '1':
        raise RuntimeError('Browser worker requires the approved Docker image')


def fixture_origin():
    require_browser()
    address = ipaddress.IPv4Address(os.environ['BMF_FIXTURE_IP'])
    if not address.is_private or address.is_loopback or address.is_link_local or address.is_unspecified:
        raise ValueError('Invalid fixture address')
    return f'http://{address}:5000'


async def run_tool(data):
    require_browser()
    action = TypeAdapter(ToolAction).validate_json(data)
    if action.name != 'browser_test':
        raise ValueError('Browser worker accepts browser_test only')
    from .tools.browser import browser_test
    async with asyncio.timeout(13):
        return await browser_test(action.arguments)


def main():
    require_browser()
    signal.alarm(150 if sys.argv[1:] == ['serve'] else 14)
    if sys.argv[1:] == ['serve']:
        signal.pause()  # PID 1 exits on expiry; Docker --init reaps children.
    elif sys.argv[1:] == ['health']:
        fixture_origin()
        print('ready')
    elif sys.argv[1:] == ['tool']:
        data = sys.stdin.buffer.read(20001)
        if len(data) > 20000:
            raise ValueError('Worker input exceeds limit')
        print(json.dumps(asyncio.run(run_tool(data))))
    else:
        raise ValueError('Unsupported browser operation')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

"""Trusted runner shipped in the reviewed image; never invoked on the Mac."""
import asyncio
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import sys
from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from .schemas import ToolAction


def require_container():
    if not os.path.exists('/.dockerenv') or os.environ.get('BMF_FIXTURE_WORKER') != '1':
        raise RuntimeError('Fixture worker requires the approved Docker image')


async def run_tool(data):
    require_container()
    action = TypeAdapter(ToolAction).validate_json(data)
    if action.name == 'http_request':
        from .tools.http import http_request
        return await http_request(action.arguments)
    if action.name == 'browser_test':
        from .tools.browser import browser_test
        return await browser_test(action.arguments)
    raise ValueError('Unsupported worker tool')


def main():
    require_container()
    if sys.argv[1:] == ['serve']:
        import signal
        signal.alarm(150)  # Container self-expires even if the API process disappears.
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('bookshelf_fixture', '/fixture/app.py')
        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        sys.modules[spec.name] = module
        spec.loader.exec_module(module)
        app = module.create_app({'DATABASE': '/tmp/bookshelf.sqlite3',
                                 'SECRET_KEY': 'isolated-fixture-only',
                                 'SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE': False})
        # Factory's root_path comes from /fixture/app.py, so templates stay there.
        result = app.test_cli_runner().invoke(args=['init-db'])
        if result.exit_code:
            raise RuntimeError('Fixture initialization failed')
        app.run(host='127.0.0.1', port=5000, debug=False, use_reloader=False)
    elif sys.argv[1:] == ['health']:
        import httpx
        response = httpx.get('http://127.0.0.1:5000/', timeout=2, trust_env=False)
        response.raise_for_status()
        print('ready')
    elif sys.argv[1:] == ['tool']:
        print(json.dumps(asyncio.run(run_tool(sys.stdin.buffer.read(20000)))))
    else:
        raise ValueError('Unsupported worker operation')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
"""Trusted, stdin-only browser dispatcher. No server or general execution API."""
import asyncio
import ipaddress
import json
import os
import signal
import sys
from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from .schemas import ToolAction


def require_browser():
    if not os.path.exists('/.dockerenv') or os.getenv('BMF_BROWSER_WORKER') != '1':
        raise RuntimeError('Browser worker requires the approved Docker image')


def fixture_origin():
    require_browser()
    address = ipaddress.IPv4Address(os.environ['BMF_FIXTURE_IP'])
    if not address.is_private or address.is_loopback or address.is_link_local or address.is_unspecified:
        raise ValueError('Invalid fixture address')
    return f'http://{address}:5000'


async def run_tool(data):
    require_browser()
    action = TypeAdapter(ToolAction).validate_json(data)
    if action.name != 'browser_test':
        raise ValueError('Browser worker accepts browser_test only')
    from .tools.browser import browser_test
    async with asyncio.timeout(13):
        return await browser_test(action.arguments)


def main():
    require_browser()
    signal.alarm(150 if sys.argv[1:] == ['serve'] else 14)
    if sys.argv[1:] == ['serve']:
        signal.pause()  # PID 1 exits on expiry; Docker --init reaps children.
    elif sys.argv[1:] == ['health']:
        fixture_origin()
        print('ready')
    elif sys.argv[1:] == ['tool']:
        data = sys.stdin.buffer.read(20001)
        if len(data) > 20000:
            raise ValueError('Worker input exceeds limit')
        print(json.dumps(asyncio.run(run_tool(data))))
    else:
        raise ValueError('Unsupported browser operation')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import json

from pydantic import TypeAdapter

class ToolRegistry:
    def __init__(self, pr, sandbox, output_dir=None):
        self.pr, self.sandbox = pr, sandbox
        self.output_dir = Path(output_dir) if output_dir else Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='bmf-regression-'))
        self.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    async def execute(self, action, state):
        action = TypeAdapter(ToolAction).validate_python(action.model_dump())
        if action.name == 'inspect_patch':
            return inspect_patch(self.pr, action.arguments)
        if action.name in ('http_request', 'browser_test'):
            return await self.sandbox.execute(action)
        if action.name == 'compare_behavior':
            return self.compare(action.arguments, state)
        if action.name == 'generate_regression_test':
            return self.generate(action.arguments, state)
        raise ValueError('Unknown tool')

    def compare(self, args, state):
        if args.hypothesis_id not in state.hypotheses:
            raise ValueError('Comparison requires an existing hypothesis')
        observations = {o.id: o for o in state.observations}
        observed = observations.get(args.observation_id)
        if observed is None or observed.status != 'ok':
            raise ValueError('Comparison requires a successful execution observation')
        refs = [observed.id]
        if args.property == 'no_browser_execution':
            if (observed.tool != 'browser_test' or observed.data.get('marker_tested') is not True or
                    type(observed.data.get('marker_executed')) is not bool):
                raise ValueError('Browser marker was not actually tested')
            holds = not observed.data['marker_executed']
            description = 'Fresh marker execution was ' + ('absent within the bounded observation window' if holds else 'observed in the browser')
        elif args.property == 'same_book_count':
            control = observations.get(args.control_id)
            if control is None or control.status != 'ok' or control.id == observed.id:
                raise ValueError('Distinct successful control observation required')
            for item in (control, observed):
                if (item.tool != 'http_request' or item.data.get('status_code') != 200 or
                        item.data.get('path') != '/' or item.data.get('method') != 'GET' or
                        type(item.data.get('book_count')) is not int):
                    raise ValueError('Successful search requests required')
            attack_action = state.actions[state.observations.index(observed)]
            control_action = state.actions[state.observations.index(control)]
            attack = attack_action.arguments.query.get('q', '')
            baseline = control_action.arguments.query.get('q', '')
            import re
            if (not baseline or not attack.startswith(baseline) or attack == baseline or
                    control.data['book_count'] != 0 or
                    not re.search(r"['\"]\s*(?:OR|UNION)\b", attack[len(baseline):], re.I)):
                raise ValueError('Search comparison requires unmatched control and its SQL-predicate variant')
            refs.append(control.id)
            holds = observed.data['book_count'] == control.data['book_count']
            description = f"Observed {observed.data['book_count']} books; stated control {control.data['book_count']}"
        else:
            if (observed.tool != 'http_request' or observed.data.get('status_code') != 200 or
                    observed.data.get('body_excerpt_truncated') is not False or not args.expected):
                raise ValueError('Complete successful HTTP response and expected text required')

import asyncio
import json
from pathlib import Path
import pytest
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, Mock
from pydantic import TypeAdapter, ValidationError
from app.browser_worker import fixture_origin, run_tool
from app.sandbox import BACKEND, SandboxError
from app.schemas import ToolAction
from conftest import run


def action(name):
    return TypeAdapter(ToolAction).validate_python({'name': name, 'arguments': {}})


def test_browser_routes_to_separate_worker(pr, docker_setup):
    sandbox, calls, state = docker_setup
    async def scenario():
        await sandbox.start(pr)
        try:
            await sandbox.execute(action('browser_test'))
            args, kw = calls[-1]
            assert args[2] == sandbox.browser and 'app.browser_worker' in args
            assert json.loads(kw['input_data']) == action('browser_test').model_dump()
            await sandbox.execute(action('http_request'))
            assert calls[-1][0][2] == sandbox.container
        finally:
            await sandbox.stop()
    run(scenario())


@pytest.mark.parametrize('failure', ['network', 'app', 'browser', 'health'])
def test_partial_start_failure_removes_all_resources(pr, docker_setup, failure):
    sandbox, calls, state = docker_setup
    state['fail'] = lambda args: (
        (failure == 'network' and args[:2] == ('network', 'inspect')) or
        (failure == 'app' and args[0] == 'run' and args[args.index('--name') + 1].endswith('-app')) or
        (failure == 'browser' and args[0] == 'run' and args[args.index('--name') + 1].endswith('-browser')) or
        (failure == 'health' and args[0] == 'exec'))
    with pytest.raises(SandboxError):
        run(sandbox.start(pr))
    assert not state['containers'] and not state['networks']


@pytest.mark.parametrize('unsafe', ['gateway', 'internal'])
def test_unsafe_network_fails_closed(pr, docker_setup, unsafe):
    sandbox, calls, state = docker_setup
    state[unsafe] = '172.30.0.1' if unsafe == 'gateway' else False
    with pytest.raises(SandboxError):
        run(sandbox.start(pr))
    assert not state['containers'] and not state['networks']


def test_cleanup_failure_retains_names_for_retry(pr, docker_setup):
    sandbox, calls, state = docker_setup
    async def scenario():
        await sandbox.start(pr)
        state['fail'] = lambda args: args[0] == 'rm'
        with pytest.raises(SandboxError):
            await sandbox.stop()
        assert sandbox.container and sandbox.browser and sandbox.network
        state['fail'] = None
        await sandbox.stop()
        await sandbox.stop()
    run(scenario())
    assert not state['containers'] and not state['networks']


@pytest.mark.parametrize('exception', [asyncio.TimeoutError, asyncio.CancelledError])
def test_tool_timeout_and_cancellation_remove_workers(pr, docker_setup, exception):
    sandbox, calls, state = docker_setup
    original = sandbox.command
    async def command(*args, **kw):
        if args[:2] == ('exec', '-i'):
            raise exception()
        return await original(*args, **kw)
    async def scenario():
        await sandbox.start(pr)
        sandbox.command = command
        with pytest.raises(exception):
            await sandbox.execute(action('browser_test'))
    run(scenario())
    assert not state['containers'] and not state['networks']


@pytest.mark.parametrize('field', ['runner_sha256', 'seccomp_sha256'])
def test_stale_browser_approval_rejected_before_execution(pr, docker_setup, field):
    sandbox, calls, state = docker_setup
    data = json.loads(sandbox.browser_manifest.read_text())
    data[field] = '0' * 64
    sandbox.browser_manifest.write_text(json.dumps(data))
    with pytest.raises(SandboxError, match='approved'):
        run(sandbox.start(pr))
    assert not any(args[0] == 'run' for args, _ in calls)


def test_cancellation_after_container_creation_removes_partial_run(pr, docker_setup):
    sandbox, calls, state = docker_setup
    original = sandbox.command
    async def command(*args, **kw):
        result = await original(*args, **kw)
        if args[0] == 'run':
            raise asyncio.CancelledError()
        return result
    sandbox.command = command
    with pytest.raises(asyncio.CancelledError):
        run(sandbox.start(pr))
    assert not state['containers'] and not state['networks']


def test_seccomp_delta_is_only_browser_sandbox_calls():
    baseline = json.loads((BACKEND / 'browser/docker-default-seccomp.json').read_text())
    profile = json.loads((BACKEND / 'browser/chromium-seccomp.json').read_text())
    assert profile['defaultAction'] == 'SCMP_ACT_ERRNO'
    extra = profile['syscalls'][len(baseline['syscalls']):]
    assert {name for rule in extra for name in rule['names']} == {'clone', 'setns', 'unshare', 'chroot'}
    profile['syscalls'] = profile['syscalls'][:len(baseline['syscalls'])]
    assert profile == baseline


def test_worker_rejects_other_tools_and_model_code(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr('app.browser_worker.require_browser', lambda: None)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match='browser_test only'):
        run(run_tool(action('http_request').model_dump_json()))
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        run(run_tool(json.dumps({'name': 'browser_test', 'arguments': {'javascript': 'evil()'}})))


def test_browser_context_enforces_origin_download_worker_and_socket_boundaries(monkeypatch):
    from app.tools.browser import browser_test
    from app.schemas import BrowserArgs
    monkeypatch.setattr('app.browser_worker.fixture_origin', lambda: 'http://172.30.0.2:5000')
    page = SimpleNamespace(
        set_default_timeout=Mock(), goto=AsyncMock(return_value=SimpleNamespace(status=200)),
        wait_for_function=AsyncMock(), evaluate=AsyncMock(return_value=False),
        url='http://172.30.0.2:5000/',
        locator=Mock(return_value=SimpleNamespace(inner_text=AsyncMock(return_value='BookShelf'))))
    context = SimpleNamespace(route=AsyncMock(), route_web_socket=AsyncMock(),
                              new_page=AsyncMock(return_value=page), close=AsyncMock())
    browser = SimpleNamespace(new_context=AsyncMock(return_value=context), close=AsyncMock())
    launch = AsyncMock(return_value=browser)
    class Playwright:
        async def __aenter__(self): return SimpleNamespace(chromium=SimpleNamespace(launch=launch))
        async def __aexit__(self, *args): pass
    monkeypatch.setattr('app.tools.browser.async_playwright', Playwright)
    async def scenario():
        await browser_test(BrowserArgs())
        assert launch.call_args.kwargs == {'headless': True, 'chromium_sandbox': True, 'timeout': 5000}

*** Add File: /Users/siddhilad/Desktop/breakfix/backend/DEPENDENCIES.md
+# Dependencies by execution environment
+
+Each `requirements.txt` declares exact direct versions. The matching
+`requirements.lock.txt` pins the complete transitive closure with SHA-256 hashes.
+Install locks with `--require-hashes`; do not use the backend lock in worker images.
+No package versions were upgraded during this split.
+
+| Environment | Python | Input / hash lock | Packages |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Backend orchestration | 3.13 | `requirements.txt` / `requirements.lock.txt` | 76 |
+| Local backend development/tests | 3.13 | `requirements-dev.txt` / `requirements-dev.lock.txt` | 83 |
+| BookShelf fixture and HTTP worker | 3.14 | `fixture/requirements.txt` / `fixture/requirements.lock.txt` | 18 |
+| Browser worker | 3.12 | `browser/requirements.txt` / `browser/requirements.lock.txt` | 8 |
+
+The backend needs FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, HTTPX and neatlogs 1.4.27. The SDK
+requires Python below 3.14 and brings its own instrumentor dependencies even when
+automatic instrumentation is disabled. Flask, Playwright and pytest are absent
+from the backend runtime lock. The development lock adds pytest and Playwright
+because unit tests inspect the browser executor with mocked browser operations.
+No host browser binaries or provider calls are needed to run those tests.
+
+The fixture needs Flask, HTTPX and Pydantic only. Its future-build recipe copies
+only schemas, the fixture worker and HTTP tool, and installs no SDK, browser,
+API server, test framework or Chromium system dependencies. The fixture dispatcher
+refuses browser actions. The browser image installs Playwright/Pydantic and their
+dependencies only, on the digest-pinned official Playwright base; its Python
+package version matches the preinstalled browsers. Both Dockerfiles enforce hashes.
+
+From the repository root:
+
+```sh
+# Deployment runtime
+python3.13 -m venv backend/.venv
+backend/.venv/bin/python -m pip install --require-hashes -r backend/requirements.lock.txt
+
+# Local tests (runtime plus development dependencies)
+backend/.venv/bin/python -m pip install --require-hashes -r backend/requirements-dev.lock.txt
+cd backend
+.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
+```
+
+To regenerate a lock without deliberately upgrading its existing pins, run from
+the repository root, using the corresponding Python version and target platform:
+
+```sh
+uv pip compile backend/requirements.txt --python-version 3.13 --generate-hashes --no-header --no-annotate --constraint backend/requirements.lock.txt --output-file backend/requirements.lock.txt
+uv pip compile backend/requirements-dev.txt --python-version 3.13 --generate-hashes --no-header --no-annotate --constraint backend/requirements-dev.lock.txt --output-file backend/requirements-dev.lock.txt
+uv pip compile backend/fixture/requirements.txt --python-version 3.14 --python-platform aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu --generate-hashes --no-header --no-annotate --constraint backend/fixture/requirements.lock.txt --output-file backend/fixture/requirements.lock.txt
+uv pip compile backend/browser/requirements.txt --python-version 3.12 --python-platform aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu --generate-hashes --no-header --no-annotate --constraint backend/browser/requirements.lock.txt --output-file backend/browser/requirements.lock.txt
+```
+
+Worker target validation covers Docker Desktop Linux ARM64. Backend validation is
+on macOS ARM64. Revalidate for other Python/platform targets before deployment.
+Pinned image digests and package hashes make dependency inputs reproducible;
+they do not guarantee identical image timestamps or vulnerability-free packages.
+
+Existing approved BookShelf images and commit attestations are unchanged. The
+fixture Dockerfile updates apply only to a future explicitly reviewed build;
+neither existing approved fixture was rebuilt. Those historical images still
+contain their original broader dependency set. Removing packages from them would
+require new image approvals, and is intentionally outside this change.
+
+The changed browser recipe/lock requires a new immutable browser-only approval.
+Both inputs are included in `app.sandbox.browser_digest()`, so changing dependency
+policy cannot silently reuse an old approval. The previous browser image remains
+available; no mutable tag or automatic build is used by the runtime.
+
+Validation: independent hash-locked Python 3.13 backend/development and Python 3.14
+fixture environments installed successfully and passed dependency checks. The
+runtime imported without Flask, Playwright or pytest. All fixture Linux ARM64
+Python 3.14 wheels were resolved/downloaded with hash verification. The new browser
+image installed its complete lock under Python 3.12 and passed `pip check`.
*** End Patch"));
